correctness.rationale: If a reduced-product class has zero reduced center-valued trace, subtracting the coordinate traces changes the representative by a norm-null sequence and produces exact coordinate trace zero. Wang’s uniform finite-von-Neumann theorem then gives one commutator per coordinate with a universal norm-product bound; reciprocal rescaling makes both factor sequences bounded, so they define quotient elements. The converse is tracial. Contractivity and the identity of the trace map on the center give the exact quotient-distance formula, and every tracial state vanishes on the commutator kernel and therefore factors uniquely through the center.
residual_risks: The proof is a short structural consequence of a very recent uniform theorem; no correctness gap was found.

The factor-ultraproduct codimension-one conclusion is a concrete natural special case.

limitations: This is a structural consequence of the 2026 uniform finite-von-Neumann commutator theorem. It concerns operator-norm reduced products/ultraproducts, not arbitrary C*-ultraproducts or tracial 2-norm ultraproducts.
